papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrtπ$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $κ_1$--$ψ$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $ψ$ intersection numbers.

papers.title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out. In particular, when the normal fan of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ is smooth and its edges satisfy a length condition, we show that the combined Gromov-Witten invariants are equal to a universal node polynomial. We also show that the higher genus Block-Göttsche polynomials of smooth toric surfaces corresponding to these $h$-transverse lattice polygons, including toric blowups beyond Hirzebruch and toric del Pezzo surfaces, are equal to a generating function of higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants.

papers.title: Finiteness of algebraic Weil-Petersson totally geodesic curves in pointed moduli spaces
papers.abstract: For every pair $(g,n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, we prove that $\mathcal M_{g,n}$ contains only finitely many closed algebraic curves that are totally geodesic for the Weil-Petersson metric. We show that every such curve is an arithmetic quadratic Teichmüller curve and has equal heights for all marked maximal cylinders in every periodic direction. Although there are infinitely many arithmetic Teichmüller curves, we can bound the degree of the associated torus covering by the crucial equal-height property. This leads to the desired finiteness statement. We also prove that quadratic Teichmüller curves are characterized by the existence of a holomorphic splitting of the logarithmic cotangent Kodaira-Spencer map. This result is the analogue of Möller and Viehweg's characterization of Kobayashi geodesics in $\mathcal A_g$.

papers.title: Mustafin degenerations of six points in the projective plane and self-duality
papers.abstract: Mustafin varieties provide a framework for degenerating the projective plane together with marked points, governed by the combinatorics of Bruhat-Tits buildings. Such limit objects are parametrized by the boundary points of a projective compactification of the moduli space of $n$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ constructed by Schaffler-Tevelev. In this paper, we study the locus of this compactification generically parametrizing self-dual configurations, or equivalently, six points lying on a conic. We prove that this locus is a tropical compactification of the moduli space of self-dual configurations, with associated fan a refinement of the self-dual tropical Grassmannian introduced by Geiger-Hashimoto-Sturmfels-Vlad. We show that this compactification is a blow up of $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,6}$ and we classify the objects it parametrizes: degenerations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ equipped with a stable $6$-pointed rational curve that records the limiting conic.

papers.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
papers.abstract: We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve $x^uy^v=0$, and the punctual Quot schemes of the module $k[[x]]^u\oplus k[[y]]^v$ over the reduced node $xy=0$. We compute their motivic generating functions for all $u,v$ and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution $\mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L}$. This proves the Hilb--Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb--Quot--HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

papers.title: Indeterminacy of period map and Griffiths heights for hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the period map $\overline {\mathcal P}$, from the GIT moduli space of degree $d$ hypersurface $X$ in $\mathbb P^n$ to the Baily-Borel compactification of the period image associated to the middle cohomology $H^{n-1}_{\rm prim}(X,\mathbb Z)$, extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has at worst nodal singularities (resp. suspensions of slc surface singularities) when $n$ is even (resp. $n$ is odd). This verifies and generalizes Laza-O'Grady's prediction on the indeterminacy locus of the period map for quartic K3s to arbitrary hypersurfaces. For Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, we prove that the birational map from the GIT moduli space to the BBH compactification extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has semi-log canonical singularities. The results apply to distinguish the Baily-Borel and BBH compactifications. In the process, we answer two questions of Mordant on the Griffiths height for families of hypersurfaces over curves, which are crucial to the proofs of the main results.

papers.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $ξ_0,\dots,ξ_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2ξ_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}ξ_0^2ξ_1+ξ_0ξ_4-ξ_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.

papers.title: Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This paper studies foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic. We provide an explicit description of all smooth foliations, linear and turbulent, and establish criteria for being $p$-closed. We explicitly determine the moduli spaces of such foliations. We give an application to the construction of $p$-closed foliations, with mild singularities, on Kummer $K3$-surfaces in positive characteristics.

papers.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,ω_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, for $X$ a rational surface, a ruled surface over an elliptic curve, a $K3$ surface, or an abelian surface, and $ρ>0$, the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$, and the same holds in characteristic zero.

papers.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
papers.abstract: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.

papers.title: An asymptotic $Γ$-BMT inequality
papers.abstract: We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $Γ$-Bayer-Macrì-Toda ($Γ$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization. For polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds, this yields a reduction of positive rank generalized Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants to those counting sheaves pure in codimension one. We further express these invariants in terms of rank one generalized DT invariants. Thus, the rank reductions of Feyzbakhsh-Thomas hold without assuming the BMT conjecture.

papers.title: Obstructions to deforming space curves lying on a complete intersection of quadrics
papers.abstract: Let $S=S_{2,\ldots,2}\subset\mathbb P^{n+2}$ be a smooth complete intersection of $n$ quadrics containing a line $E$, where $n\geq 3$, and set $D=(n-1)\mathbf h+E$, where $\mathbf h=[\mathcal O_S(1)]$. We study the deformations of smooth curves $C\in |mD|$ and their obstructions. The linear system $|D|$ defines a birational morphism $f:S\to\overline S$ that contracts $E$ to a point and realizes an unprojection in the sense of Papadakis--Reid. When $n=3$, the surface $S=S_{2,2,2}\subset\mathbb P^5$ is a $K3$ surface and $E$ is a $(-2)$-curve. We prove that the complementary open surface $S\setminus E$ admits first-order infinitesimal deformations in $\mathbb P^5\setminus E$ that are obstructed at the second order. Using these obstructions, we show that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, there exists a generically non-reduced irreducible component $W_m$ of the Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5$ of smooth connected curves in $\mathbb P^5$. Its general member $C$ lies on a complete intersection $S_{2,2,2}$ of three quadrics, satisfies $C\sim mD$, and has $h^0(N_{C/\mathbb P^5})-\dim_{[C]}\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5=3$. In contrast, when $n>3$, we prove that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, the corresponding family of curves in $|mD|$ gives rise to a generically smooth irreducible component of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^{n+2}$.

papers.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-étale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
papers.abstract: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.

papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

papers.title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
papers.abstract: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.

papers.title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
papers.abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.

papers.title: Derived categories of threefolds near the Noether line
papers.abstract: We show that derived categories of canonical stacks associated to general threefolds in the principal component of the moduli space of canonical threefolds on the refined Noether line are semiorthogonally indecomposable. First we generalize a criterion of Kawatani-Okawa for the indecomposability of derived categories of surfaces of general type to higher-dimensional varieties and stacks. And then we generalize a construction of Kobayashi and Hu-Zhang and a classification result of Coughlan-Pignatelli to the second and third Noether lines to show that our criterion applies to these canonical stacks.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlevé equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlevé equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.
